summary: Applying a lit oil lamp prints the C turn-off message, then JS stops before timer and light cleanup because timeout.c cleanup_burn requires an injected deleteObjectLightSource hook that apply.c use_lamp does not supply.

source.branch: With a carried, lit oil lamp and an attached BURN_OBJECT timer, apply.c:use_lamp calls end_burn(obj, TRUE). timeout.c:end_burn calls stop_timer, whose cleanup_burn deletes the LS_OBJECT source, restores unused fuel, clears lamplit, and refreshes inventory.
callers: apply.c:use_lamp -> timeout.c:end_burn on the already-lit branch; js/apply.js:use_lamp calls js/timeout.js:end_burn with state but without object-light cleanup hooks.
timeout.c:stop_timer -> cleanup_burn for the BURN_OBJECT timer; js/timeout.js:stop_timer preflights a required deleteObjectLightSource hook before unlinking.
dependencies: light.c:del_light_source(LS_OBJECT, obj) is implemented as js/light.js:del_light_source; wire the real source operation for timer cleanup rather than refusing when an optional injected hook is absent.
invent.c:update_inventory is called for an inventory object after cleanup; preserve its active-display conditions and source ordering.

evidence: The saved v13 evaluation at 35deeae3b45298577e919836bfad5c2da681ab6b matches 17/18 screens and stops at zero-based step 17 with timer cleanup requires deleteObjectLightSource for function 4; the fixed and earlier synthetic workload still pass.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:use_lamp (1628-1702) calls end_burn on the lit branch. Upstream timeout.c:end_burn (1804-1824) stops BURN_OBJECT and cleanup_burn (1830-1848) calls light.c:del_light_source before clearing lamplit and updating inventory.

JavaScript js/apply.js:use_lamp prints the off message then calls end_burn(obj,true,{state}). js/timeout.js:preflightTimerCleanup requires env.hooks.deleteObjectLightSource and throws before the timer is removed. js/light.js:del_light_source already implements the C light deletion. This is a production wiring defect across the source functions, not an oil-lamp-only case rule.
